title: GPU SKU + driver profiling notes (round 2)
content:
Purpose and context

This doc captures our round‑2 hands‑on investigation comparing A100 / H100 / L40S across commonly used cloud SKUs and a couple of driver/CUDA stacks. Goal: identify practical performance deltas that impact our serving runtime (latency SLOs and token throughput) and produce actionable configuration guidance for hosted and private deployments. This is an informal working note (experiments were run in multiple regions and on a small fleet).

High level takeaways (summary)
- H100 shows the best large‑model throughput and long‑sequence efficiency when running under CUDA 12.1+ with TensorRT 8.x/Transformer Engine enabled; p50 latency improvements vs A100 are modest for short sequences but p95/p99 improve on long sequences (>=2k tokens).
- A100 is the most stable across driver/CUDA stacks we tested (CUDA 11.8 + cuBLAS/cutlass heuristics) — predictable for multi‑tenant Dedicated pools.
- L40S performs well for FP32 workloads and inference with smaller models (<=13B) at lower cost SKU; it falls behind H100 on int8/TF optimized paths for large models.
- Driver/CUDA stack mismatches produce bigger variance than instance SKU choice in some cases — pin combos for production.

Test matrix (what we ran)
- GPUs / SKUs: 
  - NVIDIA A100 40GB (AWS p4d / GCP a2-standard-4 variants)
  - NVIDIA H100 80GB (AWS p5 / GCP h1-like early access)
  - NVIDIA L40S ~48GB (GCP l4 / some market SKUs)
- Driver / CUDA stacks: 
  - CUDA 11.8 driver 510.x (baseline for A100 workloads)
  - CUDA 12.1 driver 535.x (recommended for H100 Transformer Engine kernels)
  - CUDA 12.2 driver 540.x (stability test, mixed results with older Triton builds)
- Models & precisions: LLama2 7B & 13B (fp16), 70B (fp16/int8 where supported), opt-style 30B fp16
- Workloads: short chat turn (seq_len=256), medium (512), long (2048). Prompt mix: 70% short, 20% medium, 10% long to approximate typical prod traffic.
- Batch sizes tested: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 (auto batching disabled for latency SLO tests; enabled for throughput tests)
- Profiling tools: nsys (Nsight Systems), nvprof traces for kernel hotspots, nvtx annotated traces from the runtime, dcgm for GPU metrics, and our custom token‑level timing hooks in runtime.

Methodology notes
- For stable comparisons we restarted VM instances and cleared GPU caches between runs. Each test is 5 warmup iterations + 20 measured iterations; reported numbers are median of measured iterations.
- Where available, we pinned to the same CPU/GPU affinity and exclusive GPU mode to reduce noisy neighbor effects.
- We compared two runtime modes: "latency mode" (auto‑batching off, kv cache pinned to device, eager kernel selection) and "throughput mode" (batching on, sequence chunking enabled).

Representative results (selected numbers, median across runs)
- LLama2 13B, seq=512, batch=1 (latency mode):
  - A100 (CUDA11.8): p50=120ms, p95=210ms, tokens/s=950
  - H100 (CUDA12.1): p50=110ms, p95=180ms, tokens/s=1100
  - L40S (CUDA11.8): p50=140ms, p95=260ms, tokens/s=820
- LLama2 13B, seq=2048, batch=4 (throughput):
  - A100 (CUDA11.8): tokens/s=4200, GPU util avg=78%
  - H100 (CUDA12.1): tokens/s=6500, GPU util avg=88% (Transformer Engine gains visible)
  - L40S (CUDA11.8): tokens/s=3300, GPU util avg=65%
- LLama2 70B, seq=1024, batch=1, int8 path where supported:
  - A100: run unstable on our int8 build (cuBLAS fallback kernels triggered) — throughput varied a lot, not recommended for production until runtime fn fixes.
  - H100: stable with INT8 kernels when CUDA12.1+ and patched Transformer Engine; tokens/s ~ 40% higher vs fp16 on same hardware for very long sequences.

Profiling observations & bottlenecks
- Kernel hotspots: GEMM kernels (cuBLAS / cutlass) dominate overall time for large models; H100's GEMM kernels are faster but require CUDA/toolkit parity for best performance.
- Kernel launch overheads: for short sequences and batch=1, kernel launch overheads and memcpy (host<>device) dominate — opportunities to reduce copies and keep KV cache resident are highest ROI here.
- NVLink / interconnect: multi‑GPU model sharding (tensor parallelism) shows large variance across cloud SKUs. In setups with slower interconnect, communication stalls reduced effective throughput by 15–30%.
- Memory bandwidth vs compute: L40S sometimes saturates memory bandwidth earlier than A100/H100 for certain attention patterns — impacts medium sequence lengths.
- CUDA driver mismatches: running H100 kernels on older CUDA drivers produced silent fallback to slower kernels (cuBLAS fallback) which shows up as 1.5–2x slower for some ops.

Actionable recommendations
- Production pinning: define supported driver/CUDA stacks per GPU family in our onboarding docs. Example: H100 -> CUDA 12.1/driver 535.x + Transformer Engine 1.0+, A100 -> CUDA 11.8 + 510.x.
- Hosted API: for large-model/high‑latency‑sensitive workloads prefer H100-backed Dedicated pools with CUDA12.1 images. Offer A100 Dedicated for mixed/legacy workloads for stability & predictable multi‑tenant behavior.
- Private deployments: provide prebuilt images with exact CUDA/driver combos and a verification script that runs a small binary to validate fast GEMM paths (we should ship this as a small diagnostic container).
- Runtime flags: expose kernel / GEMM preferences and an opt-in Transformer Engine toggle for customers on H100. In latency mode, prefer device KV caching + copy avoidance heuristics.
- Benchmarking harness: add automated nightly runs for each SKU + driver combo so regressions are caught early (link to CI job template in linked_artifacts).

Open questions / follow ups
- Verify H100 behavior across more CUDA 12.x microversions (12.2/12.3) in a controlled environment; some cloud images ship slightly different driver stacks.
- Evaluate MIG / multi‑instance GPU modes on A100 for high‑concurrency small model workloads — could outcompete L40S at fractional GPU pricing.
- Test TensorRT fused kernels for common decoder patterns (topK+softmax fused) to see end‑to‑end latency improvements for short-turn chat.

Operational notes (bugs found)
- Found one deterministic fallback: running our int8 conversion path on A100 with CUDA11.8 resulted in cuBLAS fallback kernels (PR opened: runtime/gh#412).
- On one GCP L40S image, driver 518.x shipped with an older nvcc/ptx mismatch causing frequent kernel relaunch; remedied by 525.x driver.

Next steps (immediate)
- (Alex) Ship the small diagnostic container image and add to private deploy onboarding (T+3d).
- (Maya/Diego) Run the same matrix against p5d/p4d variants in us-west-2 and report region variance (T+1w).
- (Priya) Add the H100/CUDA12.1 baseline to nightly benchmark CI and alert on >10% regression vs baseline (T+2w).

Notes to self (experimental breadcrumbs)
- Consider auto‑downgrade of transformer engine when driver mismatch detected, but warn loudly — silent fallback is dangerous.
- We should capture nvtx spans at token level for a 1k sequence and store artifacts for triage (adds ~10MB/run).

If you want raw traces or the CSV of numbers I collected, ping me (I left them in the benchmark GCS bucket and linked the synthetic trace names in the GH PR).

-- Alex
